lines:
Responsibilities: Creates and resolves portable project-file and artifact references against the exact trusted-core-resolved workspace/repository root while preventing traversal, symlink/reparse escape, case confusion, and time-of-check/time-of-use substitution.
Owned contracts: ProjectFileRefV1 contains WorkspaceIdentityV1, normalized slash-separated relativePath, reference kind, optional expected sha256/size, and producing EventId; ArtifactRefV1 contains only CAS digest, length, media type, and descriptor hash. References never embed absolute paths, home directories, drive-specific bindings, credential locations, file handles, or implicit authority.
Ports/DTOs: CreateProjectFileRef, ResolveProjectFileRef, ResolveRepositoryPath, and ValidateArtifactRef consume ResolvedPortableRootV1 and return handle-anchored ResolvedReferenceV1 or stable Missing/Moved/HashChanged/EscapesRoot/Unsupported diagnostics. Missing references remain visible and unresolved; the resolver never searches another workspace for a similarly named file.
Defense and atomicity: rejects absolute/UNC/device paths, drive prefixes, NUL, dot-dot, alternate data streams, reserved names, separator ambiguity, and case-fold collisions. Repository-internal paths reject every symlink/reparse point. Project file reads use descriptor/handle-relative no-follow traversal where available and verify the final opened object remains beneath the root; supported in-root links require an explicit policy and race-safe final-handle validation. Writes are not exposed through this port.
Portability/NFRs: deterministic normalization, bounded path/component lengths, cancellation, low-allocation lookup, and Windows/Linux/macOS adversarial fixtures for junctions, reparse points, hard links, case folding, and rename races.
Non-responsibilities: no claim that a working directory is a sandbox, file editing, workspace authority, artifact execution, Git operation, missing-file substitution, or canonical history mutation.

data.name: Safe Project-Relative File & Artifact Reference Resolver
data.technology: Rust handle-anchored cross-platform path resolver with no-follow filesystem primitives
